claim: Public agent APIs separate registration, preparation, post/status, notifications, and release from caller-owned allocation policy.
READ/WRITE operations and success/pending/negative-error statuses match chapter polling explanations.
Basic descriptor fields are address, byte length, and device/block/file identity; default construction does not zero fields.
Coverage checks handle device identity, start ordering, unbounded sentinel, and unsigned address overflow.
Effective synchronization upgrades NONE to STRICT when metadata backend threads share agent structures.
Metadata manager starts as the last data-constructor action and stops before members are destroyed.
Registration is best effort and aggregate success requires at least one candidate success.
Local-capable registration loads a self remote-section view and rolls back the local descriptor list if that view fails.
Ordinary request creation validates paired counts and byte lengths before registered metadata population.
Ordinary backend candidates use std::set of engine pointers rather than backend creation order; corrected agent-lifecycle and request-preparation.
Prepared per-backend descriptor maps use unordered_map; default common-backend iteration does not preserve creation order.
Prepared makeXferReq honors explicit backend-list iteration, otherwise intersects unordered maps, and locks the weak remote registration reference.
Prepared request indices are converted to size_t, checked against flat bounds, and merged only for dense compatible consecutive source/destination runs.
Identical connection metadata is accepted, changed cached connection information is rejected, and failed load is not published.
Successful remote section refresh merges into a shared object; explicit invalidation or failed section load erases it and disconnects known backends.
Transfer and prepared handles weakly name remote section lifetimes; request destructor releases backend resources but does not own caller allocations.
Post rejects expired remote generation and active repost, checking completion before deciding whether another execution may start.
getXferStatus checks backend/generation only while pending and returns cached terminal status thereafter.
Refused active release returns before deleting the public handle; successful active release nulls backend handle before deletion.
Ordinary UCX range submission chooses endpoint READ or WRITE and appends endpoint flush to preserve the intended completion boundary.
UCX status drives worker progress, retains incomplete requests, and distinguishes pending notification from tracked active-message work.
Associated UCX notification is sent after successful data completion; errors clear pending notification.
UCX release warns about incomplete requests and contains a cancellation sufficiency TODO, supporting the nontransactional cleanup explanation.
getNotifs aggregates per-engine messages best effort while retaining error status; genNotif selects one usable notification engine.
POSIX preparation requires self target, local DRAM, remote FILE, and paired descriptor counts.
POSIX path registration reserves unique file identity and commits only after open; deregistration releases path reservation and owned metadata.
POSIX fd/path modes and Linux AIO/io_uring choices are bounded backend contracts with POSIX AIO deprecated.
Without background progress, libfabric status progresses active rails; CQ errors propagate, and READ notification follows completion.
Pinned libfabric plugin documents EFA-validated environment and dependency/accelerator bounds rather than universal provider certification.
Runtime Python wrapper converts contiguous tensors to byte descriptors and maps ordinary/prepared/native lifecycle phases.
Metadata package selects installed accelerator backend and aliases its real API module; similarly named type-checking stub is not runtime implementation.
Negative native post/status/release values throw translated exceptions before Python DONE/PROC/ERR fallback can return ERR.
Explicit handle release sets released flag only after successful native return; failed finalizer queues handle on agent for best-effort later cleanup.
Notification matcher polls and removes the first prefix/substring match including empty payload cases; it is not application-generation validation.
FailedActiveReleaseKeepsRequestPollable explicitly asserts pending post, refused release, successful poll, and successful later release.
Post completion observation tests cover status/repost/release and rejected repost does not create a submitted execution.
PreparedTransfersPreserveBinaryBackendParameters checks length-bearing custom parameters through prepared paths.
LoadRemoteAfterSectionError corrupts section tag, confirms peer removal, then valid reload for absent and previously present peers.
Finite/unbounded file coverage tests reject overflowing ranges and preserve nonzero-start coverage rules.
TCPStore invalidation test explicitly invalidates remote state because that metadata service has no watch.
Named tensor contiguity/scalar, consumed notification, and leaked-finalizer tests match the Python chapter claims.
Telemetry post/transfer durations share one timer start, and finish is recorded at an agent observation point.
Telemetry can use collect-only NOP exporter; classified binding failure yields no object while other factory errors propagate.
Trace plugin factory skips absent/failed requested backends and returns no tracer if none remain.
Named notification, telemetry capture/no-sink/disable, and reused notifying-write cases exist with the documented fixture scope.
Nonfitting batch tests reject whole batches and account drops by batch length.
Preparation benchmark measures descriptor conversion/registration/preparation/request construction without posting payload transfers.
Worked lab source/destination offsets and eight-byte request match actual example constants and two-observer wait condition.
